Generated from `config.md`. To change it, open Claude Code in this folder and say "Read SETUP.md and reconfigure"; do not hand-edit.

Shared instructions for the {{NAME}} scheduled tasks ([[EACH enabled routine's task id, in backticks, comma-separated]]) and the item command. The owner is {{OWNER_FULL}} ({{OWNER_EMAIL}}), called {{OWNER_SHORT}}; "the owner" below means them. Mail from or to that address is the owner's own. "Local" times and dates mean {{OWNER_TIMEZONE}}.

## Data

- Artifact: {{ARTIFACT_URL}} (use the `ArtifactData` tool; load it with ToolSearch `select:ArtifactData`).
- Collections:
  - `initiatives/<id>`: name, tier (`drive` | `fyi`), order, status (`red` | `amber` | `green` | `dormant`), status_why (one line naming what set the status), outcome, next_action, last_touch (ISO UTC), links[]. Portfolio fields: decision_needed, stakeholders[], risk, pm_move (the owner's next move, shown as "Your next move"). Keep them current when a sweep changes the picture. `tier` (after setup seeds it), `tier_set_at`, `archived` (bool) and `archived_at` are set by the owner on the page; sweeps read them and never write them (see "Tiers and routing" and "Archived initiatives").
  - `items/<id>`: initiative_id, type (`ask_to_me` | `my_commitment` | `waiting_on` | `todo`), text, counterpart, link (Outlook webLink or Teams webUrl), source (`mail` | `teams` | `manual`), created (ISO UTC of the source message), due (ISO UTC or null), state (`open` | `done` | `dropped`), closed_at, closed_by (`sweep` | `page` | `skill`; who closed it, null while open), close_note (the evidence; required when `closed_by` is `sweep`).
  - Item states: `done` = the owner completed it (eligible for weekly-report accomplishments when there is evidence). `dropped` = the owner decided not to do it (NEVER counts as an accomplishment, never resurfaced by a sweep). Both stay with `closed_at` for history.
  - `meetings/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>`: date (local), start, end (ISO UTC), subject, initiative_id, kind (`meeting` | `focus` | `ooo` | `social` | `optional` | `allday`), importance (`critical` | `high` | `normal` | `low`), prep, decision, skippable (bool), note (conflicts, reasons).
  - `wins/<id>`: date, text, source. Verified accomplishments (sent deliverables, recognition received, resolved incidents). Never log a draft or plan as a win.
  - `meta/sweep`: last_sweep_at (ISO UTC), last_sweep_kind, filter_version.
  - `meta/recommendations`: generated_at, and `queues`, `today`, `portfolio`, each `{action, why, link, item_id?, meeting_id?}`. Rewritten by every morning and weekly sweep; the afternoon check-in never writes them. Set `item_id` when the recommendation is about an item and `meeting_id` when it is about a meeting: the page retires it automatically when that item closes or that meeting ends. Never recommend a `done` or `dropped` item.
  - `meta/prefs`: written by the page only (theme, last tab, read markers). Sweeps never touch it.
  - `digests/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<am|wk>`: one per morning sweep (`am`) and per weekly run (`wk`), shown on the Digest tab. See "Digest".
  - `reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<pm|review|status>`: the afternoon check-in (`pm`), weekly review (`review`) and {{REPORT_NAME}} draft (`status`), each on its own tab. See "Reports".
  - `archive/<YYYY-MM>`: retention roll-ups. See "Retention".
- Item ids are deterministic so re-runs never duplicate: `m-` + last 16 chars of the mail message id, `tm-` + the Teams message id, `d-` + last 16 chars of a Drafts/Outbox message id. Before creating, `get` that id; if it exists, leave it (update only if the state should change). Manual items (added on the page) have random ids; never delete them.
- Never reopen an item the owner marked `done` or `dropped`.
- Pin every write with `if_version` from your read. One `batch` per sweep (max 50 writes; split if more).
- Write `meta/sweep.last_sweep_at` LAST, set to this run's start time (UTC), only after every other write succeeded.

## Tiers and routing

- The source of truth for tier is `initiatives/<id>.tier` in the database. Setup seeds it from `config.md`; after that the owner moves initiatives between Drive and FYI with the page's "Drive this" / "Move to FYI" buttons (the page also stamps `tier_set_at`). Read tier from the database every run; never write or change `tier` on an existing initiative.
- Drive = track closely, proactive nudges. FYI = track, surface only direct asks to the owner.
- Routing signals (which initiative a message belongs to; not tier assignments):
  - [[EACH initiative, Drive then FYI, one bullet each, as "`id` (name): signals"]]
- A new recurring topic with 2+ messages that fits none: [[IF allow_new_fyi: create a new initiative (the only time a sweep writes `tier`) with `{name, tier: "fyi", order: last + 1, status and status_why per "Initiative status", outcome: "", next_action, last_touch, links: [], stakeholders: [], archived: false}` and say so in the brief | ELSE: list it under "Unfiled" in the brief]]. Never create a Drive initiative; propose it instead (the owner can then move it to Drive on the page).
- Signals classify mail that passes the noise filter. A noise sender is skipped even if it matches a signal, unless the message asks the owner something by name.

## Sources and window

- Outlook: `outlook_email_search` with `query: "*"` and `afterDateTime` = last_sweep_at, NO `folderName`, paging through ALL results (follow `nextOffset` until it stops). Never restrict to the Inbox: Outlook rules move mail into subfolders, and an Inbox-only scan misses asks. Read full bodies with `read_resource` only for candidates that pass the filter. Include Sent Items.
[[GENERATE if mail.excluded_folders is not empty]]
- EXCLUDED MAIL, matched by sender and subject. The owner's Outlook rules file this mail into folders. Do NOT page through those folders to build a skip-set of message ids: a per-folder lookup on every run is slow, tends to get skipped, and marks runs partial. Instead, drop a message from the all-folder results when it matches its folder's signature below, and never read its body:
  - [[EACH excluded folder: "`folder`: signature"]]
- A folder whose signature is `none` has no single sender pattern; the `ask_to_me` rule (see "Extraction rules") keeps its mail out unless it asks the owner something by name. A message that slips past a signature still needs a direct ask to become an item, so a missed broadcast creates nothing.
[[/GENERATE]]
[[GENERATE if mail.summary_folders is not empty: one bullet per summary folder]]
- SUMMARY FOLDER (changes only, never items): `[[folder]]`: in the [[routine]] run only, read the past [[hours]] hours (`outlook_email_search` with `folderName: "[[folder]]"` and `afterDateTime` = now minus [[hours]] hours; one short positive read, not a skip-set) and add a short "[[label]]" section: one line per thread or key with what changed and who changed it, Drive initiatives first. Its mail never becomes an item: drop it from the all-folder results when it matches [[signature]]. If that folder search fails, mark it `unavailable` in `sources[]`; it does not make the sweep partial. The other runs skip this folder.
[[/GENERATE]]
[[GENERATE if mail.vip_senders is not empty]]
- VIP senders (never filtered, always read the body, treat as Drive-level asks even when routed to a subfolder): [[EACH vip as "Name <address>", comma-separated]].
- Unanswered VIP mail older than this window: once per morning sweep, also run `outlook_email_search` with `sender` = each VIP's address and `afterDateTime` = [[vip_unread_check_days]] days ago; any unread message from a VIP with no reply from the owner becomes an item.
[[/GENERATE]]
[[GENERATE if mail.check_drafts_and_outbox]]
- Drafts and Outbox (every sweep): `outlook_email_search` with `folderName: "Drafts"`, then `folderName: "Outbox"`. A reply sitting in Drafts with no sent copy (search Sent for the subject) is a `my_commitment` "Unsent draft". Anything in Outbox is a `todo` "Stale Outbox item; delete it in Outlook on the web". Read only; never send, edit or delete them.
[[/GENERATE]]
- Calendar: `outlook_calendar_search` query `*` for the target day (morning: today; afternoon and weekly: the next workday). Morning and weekly runs write one `meetings` doc per event (the afternoon only reads) with prep, the decision to land, importance, skippable flag and conflicts. Mark overlaps in `note`. Mark the single highest-leverage meeting `critical`.
[[GENERATE if teams.enabled]]
- Teams: `chat_message_search` query `*` with `afterDateTime` = last_sweep_at, paging to the end.
[[/GENERATE]]
- The owner's sent mail and own Teams messages are used to (a) detect commitments they made and (b) close `ask_to_me` items they answered.

## Extraction rules

- Every close a sweep makes writes `state`, `closed_at`, `closed_by: "sweep"` and `close_note` (who, what, when, e.g. "{{OWNER_SHORT}} replied in thread 11/12 2:14 PM").
- `ask_to_me`: a message to the owner (To:, @mention, 1:1 chat) with a question or request and no later reply from them in the same thread or chat. Close it (`done`) when a later reply from the owner exists.
- `my_commitment`: the owner wrote "I'll / I will / let me / will send / I can / set up / follow up". Set `due` if a time was stated. Close when evidence shows it happened (sent item, invite, accepted meeting).
- `waiting_on`: someone told the owner they will deliver something. Close when it arrives.
- `todo`: explicit action items for the owner from meeting recaps or their own notes.
[[GENERATE if mail.recap_senders is not empty]]
- Meeting-recap emails from [[EACH recap sender as "Name <address>", comma-separated]]: extract EVERY task whose owner includes {{OWNER_SHORT}} as a `my_commitment`, with `due` = the next occurrence of that meeting series (look it up on the calendar). Search later sent mail, Teams and recaps for evidence each one happened, and close it with that evidence.
[[/GENERATE]]
- Update the parent initiative's `last_touch` to the newest relevant message, and its `next_action` when the sweep makes the current one stale.

## Initiative status (every run that writes initiatives; all tiers)

Status counts what is actually late. A rule that turns an initiative red for any single ask a few days old leaves every Drive initiative red, so the color stops carrying signal, while FYI initiatives nobody has touched for weeks stay green. Workdays are the owner's workdays. "Old" means older than 5 workdays. Check in this order; the first match wins:
1. `red`: 1+ open item past its `due`, or 3+ old open `ask_to_me` / `my_commitment` items.
2. `amber`: 1+ old open `ask_to_me` / `my_commitment`, or 1+ open item due by the end of the next workday, or a Drive initiative with no `last_touch` in 7+ days.
3. `dormant` (FYI only): `last_touch` 21+ days ago.
4. `green`: none of the above.
- Write `status_why` with every status, naming the trigger with counts and the oldest example, e.g. "2 overdue: pricing reply (due 11/12), rollout plan (due 11/13)" or "No activity since 10/09". Rewrite it when the reason changes, even if the color does not.
- A color change is a digest `status` change (`before`, `after`, `why` = the new `status_why`). A `status_why`-only change is not.

## Archived initiatives (set by the owner on the page)

- The owner archives a finished or dormant initiative with the page's Archive button (`archived: true`, `archived_at`) and restores it with Unarchive. Sweeps read `archived` every run and never write it, exactly like `tier`.
- Skip archived initiatives in status, recommendations, the brief[[IF afternoon: , the afternoon Drive pulse]][[IF weekly: , the weekly review's stale and dormant lists]][[IF report: , and new-line suggestions for the {{REPORT_NAME}}]]. Their items stay where they are.
- New mail or Teams activity that routes to an archived initiative still becomes an item there (never drop a real ask), and the digest records it as `{kind: "archived_activity", initiative_id, item_id, text}` so the owner can decide whether to unarchive.
- Retention never deletes initiatives, archived or not.

## Recommended actions (morning and weekly sweeps write `meta/recommendations`)

Each is one concrete action, verb first, doable today, with a one-sentence why grounded in this sweep's evidence and a source link when there is one. Never recommend work on an archived initiative.
- `queues`: the single open item whose closure most helps someone waiting on the owner (prefer Drive stakeholders, unsent drafts, oldest asks).
- `today`: how to spend the day's best 30-60 minutes, usually prep for the anchor meeting or reclaiming a skippable one.
- `portfolio`: a leadership move: define an outcome, force a decision, correct the record, send the status leadership is missing, or drop or delegate a stale initiative.

## Digest (morning sweep and weekly run)

The owner reads what changed on the Digest tab, not in the run's chat. The morning sweep writes `digests/<YYYY-MM-DD>-am`; the weekly run writes `digests/<YYYY-MM-DD>-wk` (`date` = today, local; the page files a `wk` digest under the next workday). The afternoon check-in writes no digest, so the next morning's window covers the whole day.
- Write it in the sweep's pinned batch, before `meta/sweep.last_sweep_at`. A same-day re-run replaces it.
- Fields: date (local), kind (`morning` | `weekly`), generated_at, window_start (the last_sweep_at this run read), window_end (this run's start), headline (one or two sentences, the single most important change, verb-first if it is an action), changes[], summaries[] (morning only), sources[], brief_md (morning only).
- `changes[]`: one entry per change THIS run made, `{kind, item_id?, initiative_id?, text, before?, after?, why?, link?}`. Kinds: `added` (new item), `closed` (the sweep set an item to `done`; evidence in `why`, the same text as the item's `close_note`), `status` and `next_action` (initiative changes, with before/after/why), `due` (set or moved), `initiative_new`, `archived_activity` (see "Archived initiatives"), `meeting` (added, cancelled or moved since the stored copy), `win`. `text` is a short plain sentence; `why` cites who, what, when. Never list items the owner closed on the page. No change, no entry; an empty list with a headline saying "No item changes" is valid.
- `summaries[]` (morning only): the summary-folder lines as `{key, change, who, when}`. The page shows them under the heading set by `summaryLabel` in its config block.
- `sources[]`: one `{name, status, note}` per source read (Outlook, Teams, Calendar, Drafts/Outbox, VIP check, each summary folder). `status` = `ok` | `partial` | `unavailable`. Unavailable is never written as zero.
- `brief_md` (morning only): the full brief in "Brief format", plain text with line breaks.

## Reports (afternoon check-in, weekly review, {{REPORT_NAME}})

- Ids: `reports/<today>-pm` (afternoon), `reports/<today>-review` and `reports/<today>-status` (weekly). `date` = today, local. A same-day re-run replaces the doc.
- Fields: date, kind (`afternoon` | `weekly_review` | `status_report`), generated_at (ISO UTC), headline, sections[] of `{heading, lines[]}`, sources[] (same rules as the digest), body_md (the full report as plain text).
  - A line is `{text, item_id?, initiative_id?, link?, label?}`. Set `item_id` whenever the line is about an item: the page then shows the item's live state with its buttons. `label` carries the evidence label or `confirm` for anything inferred in the {{REPORT_NAME}}.
  - {{REPORT_NAME}} only: title (from the configured title format and period, see "{{REPORT_NAME}} drafting"), period_start, period_end (local dates), file_path (the local draft's path). `body_md` is the exact text of the local `status-reports/` file, and the page's Copy button copies only that (as rich text, so the bullets paste as real nested bullets). `sections` are its configured sections, one line per bullet, followed by the "For you" sections, which are never part of `body_md` or the file.
- Writing a report is not an item change: it never appears in a digest's `changes[]`, and the afternoon report is the only write the afternoon task makes.
- If a report write fails, print the full report in chat and say it was not saved.

[[GENERATE if report]]
## {{REPORT_NAME}} drafting (weekly run)

The owner already has a {{REPORT_NAME}} they edit a little each week. A draft they have to rewrite is wasted. The job is to edit their last sent {{REPORT_NAME}} for this week and show them what changed.

Periods
- THIS WEEK = the owner's work week that contains this run, first to last workday (Mon-Fri for a Mon-Fri owner), even if the run is before its last workday. NEXT WEEK = the work week after it.
- REPORT PERIOD (the title): [[IF report.title_period is completed: THIS WEEK | ELSE: NEXT WEEK]].
- Each section reads a window set by its role: `priorities` = NEXT WEEK only (never this week's work); `accomplishments` = the 7 days ending now; `blockers` = this week and NEXT WEEK; `info` = from NEXT WEEK out about 6 weeks (the owner's own OOO and holidays, dated asks of {{REPORT_AUDIENCE}}); `other` = what its prompt says.

Inputs
- [[IF previous_report_search: The last 5 sent {{REPORT_NAME}}s: `outlook_email_search` with {{PREVIOUS_REPORT_SEARCH}}. Keep hits sent by the owner whose subject starts like the title format (ignore "Re:", "Fw:" and "Disregard"). Read them in full with `read_resource`. The newest is the BASE; the older ones show how long each line has been carried. If none is found, say so in the headline and draft from scratch in the configured sections. | ELSE: No search for past {{REPORT_NAME}}s is configured, so there is no BASE: draft from scratch in the configured sections, skip the BASE-only rules (1, 7 and the length check in 4), and say so in the headline.]]
- Accomplishments: items closed `done` and `wins` in the window. An item with `closed_by: "sweep"` whose `close_note` shows only a reply means the owner answered, not that they delivered something; use it only when the close evidence is a delivered artifact.
- Priorities: open items due in NEXT WEEK or undated, each initiative's `next_action`, and NEXT WEEK's calendar (releases, deadlines, external demos, decision meetings, anything the owner presents or leads). The calendar is the main source for what NEXT WEEK holds.
[[GENERATE if mail.recap_senders is not empty]]
- This week's meeting-recap emails: decisions with dates, and risks, issues or action items owned by the owner.
[[/GENERATE]]
- Info: calendar from the first day of NEXT WEEK out about 6 weeks, searched for the owner's own OOO ("OOO", "PTO", "Out of office", events they organize shown as out of office).

Format
- Copy the BASE's layout: title line, blank line, then each configured section heading on its own line ([[EACH weekly_report.sections entry: "heading", comma-separated]]), with "- " bullets indented two spaces per level. Short fragments in the owner's voice, no citations, no evidence labels in the text[[IF style.no_em_dashes: , no em dashes]]. Mark anything inferred "(confirm)".

Rules
1. Carry forward. Start from the BASE, in its order and wording, except the self-written sections (rule 6), which start empty. Change a line only when evidence moved it: rewrite its sub-bullet as the next step, add a line for new work, and take out lines whose work finished (they move to the accomplishments section). A sub-bullet that only reports past news ("released 10/21") is not a priority: replace it with the next step or take the line out. Every line taken out is listed in "For you: changes vs last {{REPORT_NAME}}" with why; the file stays paste-ready with no "(remove)" markers. A line with no news stays as written.
2. Portfolio-wide. The {{REPORT_NAME}} covers every initiative the owner reports on, whatever its tier. Tier decides what {{NAME}} puts in front of the owner; it never removes a line. Add a new top-level line only for a Drive initiative or a topic with 2+ touches from the owner this week, marked "(confirm)".
3. Connect new to existing. New work that belongs to a line already on the list goes under it as a sub-bullet, not as a new top-level line; say so in "For you: changes vs last {{REPORT_NAME}}".
4. Detail level. Priorities are themes with short sub-bullets: no meeting clock times, no per-line owners, a date only for a release, deadline, external demo or decision. Keep the section about the BASE's length (within about 20%). Accomplishments: 3 to 5 bullets (never more than 6), each starting with a result verb (Released, Completed, Validated, Delivered, Decided), with a number where one exists and a link where a shareable artifact exists. Merge related items. Team results count. Recognition received (from `wins`) is a candidate. A draft, demo, PR or plan is not delivered, and `dropped` items never appear.
5. Info (the `info` section; if there is none, the `blockers` section; else the last section). The owner's OOO with dates, or "No OOO planned through MM/DD" when the search finds none. Things waiting on {{REPORT_AUDIENCE}}, and "Deprioritized:" for any Drive item the owner dropped this week, no spin. Never metrics or other people's availability unless the section's prompt asks for them.
6. Sections the owner writes themselves ([[EACH section with self_written: true, as "heading", comma-separated, or "none"]]): leave them empty in the draft. The only exception is something the owner already stated in writing to {{REPORT_AUDIENCE}} this week: paraphrase it, marked "(confirm)". Put suggestions in "For you: to consider". Never {{NAME}} counts, never anything about a named person's performance, never feelings the owner did not express.
7. Stale lines. A BASE line with the same wording in 4+ consecutive sent {{REPORT_NAME}}s and no item, mail or Teams activity in 4 weeks is stale: keep it as written and list it in "For you: stale lines" with the week count and "Keep, park, or drop?".
8. Overdue. An open item whose due date passed before NEXT WEEK is not a priority. List it in "For you: overdue" with its due date.

"For you" sections (report doc only, after the configured sections; never in `body_md` or the file; omit an empty one)
- "For you: changes vs last {{REPORT_NAME}}": one line per change (updated, added, moved to accomplishments, connected, taken out), each with a short why and the evidence link.
- "For you: stale lines" (rule 7), "For you: overdue" (rule 8), "For you: to consider" (blockers and risks for this week and NEXT WEEK, and rule 6 suggestions).
- "For you: talking points": 2 or 3 decisions or asks for {{REPORT_AUDIENCE}}, grounded in this week's evidence.
[[/GENERATE]]

## Afternoon check-in (no item changes)

The afternoon task is a check-in, not an update. It reads the database, mail, Teams and the next workday's calendar with the same sources, folders and noise filter, and saves only `reports/<today>-pm`: no items, initiatives, meetings, recommendations, digests or `meta/sweep`, and it never advances `last_sweep_at`. Anything new is picked up by the next morning sweep.

## Retention (weekly run only, after the {{REPORT_NAME}} draft; keeps the database far below its 25,000-record cap)

- `meetings`: delete docs whose `date` is more than 7 days ago.
- `items` closed more than 30 days ago: append `{id, initiative_id, type, text, state, closed_at}` to `archive/<YYYY-MM>.entries[]` (one doc per month), then delete the item.
- `wins` older than 120 days: roll into `archive/<YYYY-MM>.wins[]`, then delete.
- `digests` older than 14 days: delete. `reports`: delete `-pm` older than 14 days, `-review` and `-status` older than 180 days. Never touch local `status-reports/` files.
- Never delete open items, initiatives, `meta/*`, or open manual items. Report counts deleted and archived, plus the total document count, in the weekly review.

## Guardrails (HARD)

- Read-only on mail and Teams. NEVER call outlook_send_mail, outlook_send_draft, outlook_create_draft, outlook_create_reply_draft, outlook_create_reply_all_draft, outlook_update_draft, outlook_forward_mail, outlook_modify_labels, outlook_modify_thread_labels, outlook_batch_modify_labels, outlook_create_filter, outlook_create_event, outlook_update_event, outlook_delete_event, outlook_respond_to_event, outlook_set_vacation, teams_send_chat_message, teams_send_channel_message, teams_reply_channel_message, teams_create_chat, or any mail, Teams or calendar delete or trash tool. (Retention's `ArtifactData` deletes in this assistant's own database are allowed.)
- Never launch or automate an Outlook client (classic, new, or Outlook on the web) for any reason. A dormant client can send stale queued Outbox mail the moment it opens.
- The only writes allowed are to this artifact's database (per the rules above) and to this folder's `status-reports/`.
- Connection failure means data unavailable, not zero. If Outlook or Teams search fails, say so and do NOT advance last_sweep_at.
- Label status claims VERIFIED (read this run) / INFERRED / UNKNOWN. A draft, demo, PR or plan is never described as delivered.
[[GENERATE if confidentiality is not empty]]
- [[EACH confidentiality rule, one bullet each]]
[[/GENERATE]]

## Brief format (stored in the morning digest's `brief_md`)

Chat output for the morning run is only: the digest headline, one line of counts (added / closed / status changes), any unavailable source, and the {{NAME}} link. If the batch carrying the digest fails, print the full brief in chat instead and say it was not saved.

Style: concise, no filler[[IF style.no_em_dashes: , no em dashes (use " -- ")]][[IF style.extra: ; style.extra]]. Sections in order, omit empty ones:
[[IF routines.morning.joke: 0. One short, genuinely funny, work-safe joke or pun.]]
[[IF report and previous_report_search: 0b. {{REPORT_NAME}} check (first workday after the weekly run only). Run `outlook_email_search` with {{PREVIOUS_REPORT_SEARCH}} and `afterDateTime` = the weekly run's day, 00:00 local. If the owner has sent it (not a "Re:", "Fw:" or "Disregard"), omit this section. If not: one line "{{REPORT_NAME}} not sent yet" pointing to its tab, then up to 3 lines on what changed since the draft that they may want to add (items closed `done`, new `wins`, new asks from {{REPORT_AUDIENCE}}). Read only; never rewrite the draft or its report doc.]]
1. Top 3 today (Drive first; each a verb-first action with who and why now).
2. Replies owed (oldest first, age in days, link).
3. My commitments open (due first).
4. Waiting on (2+ days old only, unless due today).
5. Calendar prep: per meeting, what it is for, which initiative, what to bring or decide; mark low-value meetings as skippable candidates with a one-line reason.
[[EACH summary folder whose routine is morning: 5b. "label": one line per key, what changed and by whom.]]
6. Item changes this run: counts added / closed, new initiatives.
[[IF not allow_new_fyi: 7. Unfiled: recurring topics (2+ messages) that fit no initiative, one line each, so the owner can decide where they go.]]
End with the {{NAME}} link: {{ARTIFACT_URL}}
